title: Eleven Small Charges. One Big Number.
idea: A man adds up eleven small monthly charges he said yes to one evening at a time; the pain of paying never came

cast.name: Arlo
cast.look: tall man in a mustard sweater, short dark hair, always holding a phone

cast.name: Jo
cast.look: his friend, teal hoodie, hair in a bun, a mug in her hand

scenes.title: The statement
scenes.place: Arlo's small apartment, a lamp on, he sits on the couch with a laptop open on a card statement

lines.t: Arlo opened his card statement and counted eleven things he never remembered buying.
Each one was small. None was over sixteen dollars.
Read them out loud.
A film app. A music app. Cloud space. A meal box. I ate that once.
By the end of this evening, he would know the one number he had never seen.

scenes.title: A Tuesday
scenes.place: Arlo's kitchen on a Tuesday evening, a phone propped against a fruit bowl showing a free trial banner

lines.t: It started on a Tuesday. A film app offered seven days free.
Free? Sure. I'll cancel before it renews.
He did not cancel. After the free week it cost five dollars a month, charged on the same day, every month.
Nothing felt different. Money left his account, and he felt nothing at all.

scenes.title: A Friday
scenes.place: Arlo's desk at the window on a Friday night, a phone showing a storage full warning

lines.t: Then a Friday. His phone said the storage was full.
Twelve dollars for more space? Fine. It's just space.
It was easy. One tap, and the problem went away.
A music app came the same way. A meal box came after a long week.
Each yes took less than ten seconds, on a different evening.

scenes.title: A Sunday
scenes.place: Arlo's cramped kitchen on a Sunday afternoon, a laptop open on a meal box sign-up page, a half-empty fridge behind him

lines.t: The meal box was a Sunday. Four dinners a week, and the first box was half price.
Half price? I'll pause it after the first one.
He forgot to pause it. The box renewed on the same date every month, and most months he was out of town.
Out of town, and still paying for dinners.
That is how an eleventh charge arrives. Not in one big yes. In ten small ones, and a forgotten pause.

scenes.title: The name
scenes.place: A chalkboard in a classroom corner with a coin on one side and a sealed envelope on the other

lines.t: Researchers who study spending have a name for what he did not feel. The pain of paying.
Handing over cash stings. A card tap stings less. A charge that repeats on its own barely registers.
It does not mean people are foolish. It describes how the sting fades when payment is automatic and small.

scenes.title: Eleven
scenes.place: Arlo's couch again, the laptop now showing a plain list of eleven lines with a calculator beside it

lines.t: Back on the couch, Jo helped him add the lines.
Five. Fourteen. Twenty-six. Keep going.
Ninety-one dollars. Every month.
Ninety-one? I never spent ninety-one on anything.
Twelve months of it was one thousand, ninety-two dollars.

scenes.title: Which ones
scenes.place: The same couch at midnight, Arlo has a pen and circles items on a printed copy of the list

lines.t: Which ones did you use this month?
The music app. The cloud space. Maybe the film app. Once.
If someone asked for ninety-one dollars at once, would you have said yes?
No. Not in one go. Never.
That is the trick of small. Nothing was hidden. It was only spread across eleven dates.
Three of the eleven. The other eight had been paid for months, each one quietly.
He crossed out five that night, and left the rest on his list to think about.
It's strange. The charges were never big. It was the adding that hurt.

scenes.title: The question
scenes.place: A close view of the printed list on the coffee table with a pen lying across it

lines.t: No single charge ever felt like a decision. Together, they were a year of them.
Arlo kept the printed list on the fridge.
Which of the eleven would you have kept?
